summary: Ernst Krebs Sr. and Jr. marketed laetrile, an apricot-pit cyanide compound, as a cancer cure from the 1950s; the John Birch Society made it a far-right freedom cause as patients, including children, died.
keywords: Committee for Freedom of Choice in Cancer Therapy

evidence.note: Krebs Sr. turns to a Washo herbal remedy and sells Leptinol syrup during the 1918 flu pandemic
per the official story, Krebs Jr. turns his father's compound into laetrile in 1949
long biography of Krebs Jr.: failed medical school, honorary doctorate from an unaccredited Bible college
McNaughton, Canadian gun-runner, funds laetrile and builds factories in seven countries from 1961
Cecile Hoffman goes from Montreal to Tijuana, where Ernesto Contreras starts prescribing laetrile
McNaughton convicted of stock fraud in Canada, moves to Tijuana to run clinics and smuggling
John Birch Society enters in 1972 behind Dr. John Richardson; Bradford builds a national committee
Birchers make medical freedom a conservative issue and push state legalisation laws
children die of cyanide poisoning in 1977 after taking laetrile
Chad Green and Joseph Hofbauer: parents pull children from chemo for laetrile, courts split on parental rights
Steve McQueen dies in 1980 after laetrile treatment in Mexico; later trials find no benefit
laetrile still sold as vitamin B17 in Mexican clinics; links drawn to RFK Jr. and ivermectin

notes: Primary subject is the drug, so roles are empty although the Krebses would be quack-fake-healer. Birth years from general knowledge (Krebs Jr. 1911; a source title in the description says 1912). Transcript says Krebs Jr. died in 1966; context shows 1996. 1830s amygdalin and 1890s trials treated as background. reaches_present rests on the RFK Jr. framing and the closing segment. child-abuse here means medical neglect of children by parents.
